classification.difficultyReason: Select all applicable quadrilaterals from a supplied list using familiar properties, distinguishing one qualifying pair from both pairs where needed; no proof or new construction is required.

content.prompt: From the list – trapezium, isosceles trapezium, parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square, kite – name the quadrilaterals that have:

answer.short: Parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square; kite (one pair only).
answer.worked: A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite angles equal, as do its special cases: a rhombus, rectangle and square. A kite has one pair of opposite angles equal, between the unequal sides.
An isosceles trapezium and a rectangle have equal diagonals. A square inherits this property from a rectangle.
The diagonals of a rhombus and a kite are perpendicular. A square is also a rhombus, so its diagonals are perpendicular.
Each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angles at its endpoints. A square has the same property. A general kite has only one diagonal that bisects its endpoint angles.

answer.short: Parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square; trapezium and isosceles trapezium (one pair only).
answer.worked: A parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle and square have two pairs of parallel opposite sides. A trapezium and an isosceles trapezium have one pair.

answer.short: Parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square; trapezium, including isosceles trapezium (two pairs only).
answer.worked: Co-interior angles between parallel sides sum to $180^\circ$. Every adjacent pair is supplementary in a parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle or square. In a trapezium, including an isosceles trapezium, the two pairs along the non-parallel sides are supplementary.
